decisions.title: OpenStreetMap as the primary boundary source
decisions.decision: Use the Geofabrik OSM extract (admin_level 4/5/6 plus coastline) as the boundary source
decisions.rationale: The most recent and most precise open source available (coastline at ~1e-7 degree precision, INS geocodes on delegations and sectors); HDX COD-AB and geoBoundaries derive from the same 2014-era INS data and older OSM snapshots

decisions.title: UTM zone 32N projection for SVGs
decisions.decision: Project all SVGs with EPSG:32632 (WGS84 / UTM 32N); publish GeoJSON/TopoJSON in WGS84
decisions.rationale: Tunisia (7.5-11.6 E) sits entirely within UTM zone 32; it is conformal with very low distortion and a standard EPSG code that users can reproduce

decisions.title: Python extraction plus Node generation
decisions.decision: pyosmium/shapely for extraction (output committed in data/source); Node + mapshaper for the generation and tests
decisions.rationale: pyosmium assembles OSM multipolygons robustly; mapshaper is best-in-class for topology-aware simplification; committing the source means contributors only need Node to rebuild the maps

decisions.title: Exact nesting through planar face overlay
decisions.decision: Node all admin boundaries into planar faces; units are unions of faces; gaps allocated by nearest-boundary Voronoi within the parent
decisions.rationale: Guarantees zero overlaps and gaps and identical shared borders across levels, which the raw OSM levels do not (lakes are excluded at the lower levels; there are superseded relations)

decisions.title: Licensing split
decisions.decision: Code under MIT; data and maps under ODbL 1.0 with the attribution (c) OpenStreetMap contributors
decisions.rationale: The geometry is derived from OSM, which requires ODbL for derived databases and attribution for produced works
alternatives: CC BY 4.0 (not compatible with the OSM source)

decisions.title: Municipality boundaries come from OSM boundary=municipality relations
decisions.decision: Build the municipalities partition from the OpenStreetMap relations tagged boundary=municipality in the same Geofabrik extract (2026-10-16), clipped to the land, overlaps given to the smaller relation, no geometry invented; ids are municipality-<OSM relation>.
decisions.rationale: Same source and licence as every other layer (ODbL 1.0, © OpenStreetMap contributors), so no new licence terms. The extract holds 338 valid relations (of 350 municipalities in the 2016 division) covering 97.9% of the land in all 24 governorates; admin_level 8 in the extract only holds Algerian communes. No INS municipality code is present in OSM (5 of 338 carry ref:tn:codegeo), so the OSM relation id is the stable identifier.

decisions.title: Tifinagh names: OSM first, else letter-by-letter transliteration of the Arabic name; English: ASCII Latin name with English generic terms
decisions.decision: labeled-tfng writes name_tfng: the first Tifinagh-only value of name:zgh, name:zgh-Tfng, name:ber, name:ber-Tfng, name:tzm(-Tfng), name:shi-Tfng, name:kab-Tfng on the unit's OSM object (scripts/extract/tifinagh.py -> data/source/tifinagh-names.json, ODbL), else the Arabic name transliterated into Neo-Tifinagh with IRCAM letters (scripts/build/names.js: consonants 1:1, alef/ta marbuta -> ⴰ, glides by position, article assimilating to sun letters, no schwa); name_tfng_source records osm or transliterated. labeled-en writes name_translit: curated English name for country/regions/districts/governorates, else the labeled-mode Latin name, water generics in English (Lake X, X Dam, X Lagoon), accents removed to plain ASCII. Mode ids labeled-tfng and labeled-en, same levels as labeled; xml:lang und-Tfng / en.
decisions.rationale: Only 11 published units have a Tifinagh name in OSM (country + 10 cities) and Tunisia has no official Tifinagh nomenclature, so a transliteration is the only way to label every unit without inventing or translating names; marking the source keeps it honest. Transliterating from Arabic gives exact consonants and matches the OSM name:zgh/ber values where they follow IRCAM spelling (Tunis, Sousse, Tozeur). For English, Arabic-to-Latin needs vowels Arabic does not write, and respelling French digraphs (ou->u, ch->sh) yields forms no English source uses (Susse, Buzid), so the established Latin spelling in ASCII with English generic terms is what English-language maps use.
alternatives: Wikidata zgh/ber labels (needs network, equally sparse)
English respelling of French digraphs (dj->j, ch->sh, ou->u/w)
Leave units without an OSM Tifinagh name unlabelled
